newsitem.title: UK: UK funds upbeat, business seen growing - CBI survey.
newsitem.headline: UK funds upbeat, business seen growing - CBI survey.

text.p: Business confidence among British fund managers has strengthened for the sixth quarter running, reflecting reported and expected rises in volume of business, a survey from the Confederation of British Industry shows.

Volume of business has continued to rise strongly in the last three months, with a further though less marked increase expected over the coming qaurter, the survey, conducted by Coopers & Lybrand between August 23 and September 11, said.
The value of fees, commissions or premiums rose meoderately over the past three months but the value of interest was broadly flat. Both are seen rising in the next three months.
Total operating costs rose while average operating costs again saw a modest decrease, the survey said.
Overall profitability in the sector continued to rise for the fifth consecutive survey, due in part to the strong rise in volume of business and the value of fee and commission income.
Employment in the industry also rose markedly in the past three months, but less marked rises are expected over the next quarter.
The survey identifies domestic competition as the most likely constraint on business prospects over the coming year.
The most important motive for capital expenditure was seen as a need to increase efficiency and provide new services.
Capital spending on information technology is expected to rise significantly in the next year, with intentions the most buoyant since December 1993, the survey showed.
